summary: E2E tested the new Backup & Restore feature (local export/import + Emergent Object Storage cloud backups + nightly cron). Backend: 13 new pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_backup.py — all pass (export gzip/headers/14 collections, import roundtrip + 4 bad-archive edge cases, full cloud lifecycle push→list→download→restore→delete→404s, unknown-id 404s, staff 403 on all 7 endpoints, cron 401/401/200 with row trigger='cron'). Regression suite backend_test.py (26 tests) still passes after restores, so no data loss. Frontend: owner login → /settings shows backup-panel; download triggers a real .json.gz download; push-to-cloud creates a new backup-row with working download/restore/delete icon buttons; window.confirm flows work; delete removes the row; corrupt-file upload surfaces the backend 400 message in a toast without reloading; cloud restore reloads and app data stays intact; staff (mike@garage.com) is redirected from /settings to / and BackupPanel is not rendered; panel renders legibly in both light and dark themes.

minor.issue: Object Storage calls use blocking `requests` inside async endpoints (timeouts up to 180s) — blocks the FastAPI event loop during push/download/restore. Wrap in run_in_threadpool or use httpx.AsyncClient.
200MB size guard is applied AFTER the whole upload is read into memory (await file.read()); a huge file still balloons memory before rejection.
Background task failures are only logged; the endpoint always returns 200 so cron monitoring can never see a failed nightly backup.

action_items: Optional: offload blocking requests calls in backup.py to a threadpool (event-loop blocking during cloud push/restore).
Optional: take an automatic pre-restore snapshot — restore_snapshot() delete_many()s all 14 collections (incl. users) with no rollback if insert_many fails midway.
Cleanup: remove dead code _require_owner_factory/_require_owner globals in backup.py.
critical_code_review_comments: restore_snapshot() is non-atomic and destructive: it wipes every managed collection before inserting; a partial failure (bad doc, BSON error) leaves the DB empty with no rollback path.
Restoring an old snapshot rewrites the `users` collection, which can delete the currently-logged-in owner / password changes — worth an explicit warning in the confirm() text.
backup.py module-level `router` means register_routes() is only safe to call once; a second call would duplicate routes.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Created and soft-deleted transient cloud backup rows; 2 pre-existing cloud rows (1 manual, 1 cron) left in db.backups so the list UI is non-empty.
test_credentials: owner admin@garage.com/admin123, staff mike@garage.com/mike1234, cron token from backend/.env WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_backup.py has a module-scoped `pristine` fixture that exports the DB first and re-imports it at the end, so running it is safe. Note: writing files under /app/backend triggers uvicorn hot reload and drops in-flight HTTP connections — sleep a few seconds after creating test files before running pytest. Theme is stored in localStorage key 'garage_theme' (light/dark/system) and the toggle cycles system→light→dark.
rca_of_the_issue: Initial run showed 2 connection-aborted failures; root cause was backend hot reload triggered by creating the test file inside /app/backend, not an application defect. Re-run after reload was clean.
